pitchIn60s: What-IF is an MCP connector, a skill and a no-AI /try page for Berlin cafés, in German, English, Spanish and Polish. It turns 'Was wäre, wenn ich einen Mittagstisch anbiete?' into a six-step visual lesson. Every number is labelled as yours, calculated, a guess or imagined. Code does every sum, net of the 2026 VAT, with each line checkable. You guess the break-even before it is revealed, then move a slider that explains why the result changes. Imagined Kiez customers produce questions, not forecasts. The report ends in a printable 10-day test with a keep, tweak or stop rule agreed in advance, and an after-the-test page compares reality with the three guesses. It teaches the method and the limits of AI, and it is honest and polished. The gaps: in the demo the AI itself does nothing visible, there is no live link or judge code yet, and no real owner has used it.
standout: The closed learning loop. A test card with a rule agreed before any results, then /r#demo-result: the measured 6 a day sits on the same line as the guesses 3, 8 and 15. The pre-agreed rule gives 'Anpassen', and the page says 'Fangen Sie nächstes Mal bei 6 an'. Predicting, testing and checking is what a chatbot never does.
weakest: Use of AI in what a judge can click. The landing says 'Die KI redet', but the demo's own card says 'Von einer KI: in dieser Demo gar nichts', the rehearsal is rule-based, and the Claude-played run is not shipped.
